sections.h2: What kind of county is Hardin County, Kentucky, for a seller dealing with property tax?
sections.html:
Hardin County had 113,482 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, up 2.5 percent from the 2020 count, with Elizabethtown as both county seat and largest city. It was formed in 1792 from Nelson County, and it borders nine counties, more than any other county in the state. Courthouse fires in 1864 and 1932 destroyed county records, and the present courthouse dates from 1934.

Fort Knox dominates the local economy, and its housing sits in Hardin County. Cities in the county are Elizabethtown, Radcliff, Vine Grove, Sonora, Upton, West Point and Muldraugh, mostly in Meade County, and each town can add its own tax on top of the county bill. Two school districts levy separately: Hardin County Schools covers most of the county, while Elizabethtown Independent Schools serves most of the city of Elizabethtown.

The Census counts 51,149 housing units, 432 building permits in 2025 and 62.6 percent owner occupancy, so the market is large enough that an assessment conference can lean on recent sales near your street.

sections.h2: Which Hardin County offices bill, assess and collect property tax?
sections.html:
The Hardin County Sheriff's Office collects, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values, and the County Clerk handles anything delinquent. All three work out of the government building on North Provident Way in Elizabethtown.

  • Sheriff's Office, tax department: 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101, Elizabethtown, KY 42701. Call 270-765-5133 and choose option 1.
  • PVA: 270-765-2129, with an online record search, a tax estimator and an exemption page.
  • County Clerk: 150 N Provident Way, Suite 103, at 270-765-2171, open weekdays from 7:45 am to 4:30 pm. The clerk gives the payoff on any delinquent prior year bill.

Two cities collect their own tax separately. If your bill shows Tax District 03, the City of Radcliff bills a separate amount at 270-351-4714, and District 06 means the City of Vine Grove at 270-877-2422.

sections.h2: What is the 2026 tax calendar for Hardin County bills?
sections.html:
The sheriff posts a schedule for bills due beginning November 1, 2026, which cover the assessment as of January 1, 2026. Kentucky law sets a November 1 discount date, but the sheriff's posted calendar for these bills stretches the discount across all of November.

  • Discount period: November 1 through November 30, 2026.
  • Face amount: December 1 through December 31, 2026.
  • 5 percent penalty: January 1 through January 31, 2027.
  • 21 percent penalty: February 1 through April 15, 2027.

The office does not accept partial payments on a current year bill, but one payment can cover several bills if you attach a copy of each. A receipt comes back if you enclose a stamped, self addressed envelope. Card payments online or in person carry a 2.49 percent fee. If no bill has arrived by early November, call the sheriff and a duplicate goes out, or print one from the website's tax bill search.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 real estate tax rates in Hardin County?
sections.html:
Rates are set per $100 of assessed value, and the school district decides which line applies to your house. The PVA's 2026 schedule is summarized below in cents per $100.

Hardin County 2026 real estate rates per $100 of assessed value, from the Hardin County PVA
Tax districtStateSchoolCountyTotal
Hardin County School10.3065.2010.7090.35
Elizabethtown Independent School10.3087.3010.70112.45

Totals also include small agricultural extension, health and soil lines. City rates for 2026 appear separately: Radcliff 12.9 on real estate, Vine Grove 16.3, Sonora 20.0, Upton 25.0 and West Point 26.8. Commercial and telecommunication property in the Industrial Taxing District (District 00) pays an extra ten cents per $100 under a 2023 ordinance.

As an illustration, the Census median owner occupied value of $225,800 at the Hardin County School rate of 90.35 cents produces about $2,040 before exemptions, city tax, fire fees or 911 fees. In the Elizabethtown Independent district the same value comes to about $2,539.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Hardin County assessment?
sections.html:
Hold a conference with the PVA office before or during the inspection period, which opens on the first Monday in May and runs thirteen days. The PVA says the dates are published each year in the News-Enterprise and printed on any assessment notice you receive.

If the conference ends in agreement, you are done. Otherwise file the appeal form with the Hardin County Clerk's Office, which schedules a hearing before the county board of assessment appeals. The state notes that the board sits between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends, and that you must file by the next workday after inspection closes. A board decision you still dispute can go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Gather sale prices of similar houses in your neighborhood before the conference. In Elizabethtown, the higher Independent school rate means each dollar of assessed value costs more, so a successful appeal saves more there than in the county district.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for a homestead exemption in Hardin County?
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who live in the home may apply through the Hardin County PVA. The PVA's rate page lists the homestead and disability exemption at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, up from $46,350 for 2023 and 2024.

The amount is taken off assessed value, not off the bill itself, so the actual saving depends on your rate. At the Hardin County School total of 90.35 cents, a $49,100 reduction is worth about $444 a year. The sheriff's page sends exemption questions to the PVA at 270-765-2129, and the Department of Revenue explains that the exemption is tied to the owner, so a buyer must apply separately after closing.

sections.h2: How are Hardin County taxes split at a closing?
sections.html:
The bill covers one calendar year and is issued to the January 1 owner. The sheriff's page explains that a closing agent or attorney usually calculates each party's share and either pays the sheriff at the table or credits the buyer or seller on the settlement statement.

The sheriff will not accept a pro rated payment. One or both parties must pay the full bill, so a seller who closes in June should confirm who sends the money and when. If the house sold or transferred after January 1, bills normally go in care of the new owner, although a sale close to the printing date may not be updated in time. Forward any bill that arrives at your old address to the new owner.

sections.h2: What if a Hardin County bill goes delinquent?
sections.html:
After close of business on April 15, unpaid bills move from the sheriff to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency. Call 270-765-2171 for a payoff. The Department of Revenue shows how the total climbs: a $1,000 bill becomes $1,254 on transfer once the penalty, sheriff fee and commission are added, then picks up interest of 1 percent a month plus clerk and attorney commissions.

The clerk's website has a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information. A seller who owes back taxes can still close, because the title company pays the certificate from proceeds. Owners who would rather skip repairs and a listing can ask a cash buyer for an offer and compare it against the payoff.

faqs.q: What is the discount period for Hardin County property tax bills issued in 2026?
faqs.a: The sheriff lists November 1 through November 30, 2026 as the discount period. Face amount is due December 1 through December 31, then penalties begin in January 2027.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Hardin County tax bill in installments?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's office states that the statute does not allow partial payments on current year collections. You can pay several bills with one check if you attach copies of each.

faqs.q: How much extra does paying a Hardin County bill by card cost?
faqs.a: The sheriff charges a 2.49 percent fee on the total bill for card payments made online or at the office. Mailing a check to 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101, avoids that fee.

faqs.q: Where do I get a payoff for a delinquent Hardin County bill?
faqs.a: The Hardin County Clerk's office at 270-765-2171. Delinquent prior year bills are held there after April 15, and the clerk's website also offers a delinquent tax calculator.

faqs.q: Which Hardin County cities charge their own property tax?
faqs.a: The county's 2026 rate schedule lists Elizabethtown, Radcliff, Sonora, Upton, Vine Grove and West Point. For Radcliff (District 03) and Vine Grove (District 06), the sheriff directs payers to the city offices for separate city tax bills.
